title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal charges in the killing of UnitedHealthcare’s CEO
facts: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty in Manhattan federal court to interstate stalking charges resulting in death.
Luigi Mangione admitted to shooting UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan on December 4, 2024.
Luigi Mangione posed as a prospective investor managing $50 billion to discover the location of the corporate conference.
Luigi Mangione stated his motivation stemmed from his experiences as a patient seeking care for a back injury.
Brian Thompson's family attended the federal court plea proceeding in Manhattan.
Federal prosecutors announced they will recommend a sentence of life imprisonment for Luigi Mangione.
Luigi Mangione is scheduled for formal federal sentencing on December 18.
Defense attorney Karen Friedman Agnifilo filed a motion to dismiss New York state charges under double jeopardy protections.
Luigi Mangione entered an open guilty plea without a plea agreement before US District Court Judge Margaret Garnett.
James McDonald serves as the United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York.
Luigi Mangione was arrested at a McDonald's restaurant in Pennsylvania on December 9, 2024.
Police discovered a notebook detailing anti-healthcare industry grievances in Luigi Mangione's backpack.
Investigators recovered bullet shell casings at the crime scene inscribed with the words 'delay', 'deny', and 'depose'.
A federal judge previously dismissed two capital counts against Luigi Mangione earlier in the year.
Luigi Mangione was charged with second-degree murder and firearms crimes in New York state court.
